speaker: idera
text: Welcome to RootPath, your free tutor on any phone.

speaker: idera
text: For English, press 1. For Pidgin, press 2. For Yoruba, press 3. For Igbo, press 4. For Hausa, press 5.

speaker: idera
text: Which subject? Press 1 for Maths. Press 2 for Physics. Press 3 for English.

speaker: idera
text: Which topic is hard for you?

speaker: idera
text: I will ask a few short questions to find where the problem really starts. Press the number of your answer.

speaker: idera
text: x plus 1 over 2 equals 3 over 4. x equals what?

speaker: idera
text: Undo with the opposite: plus with −, times with divided by .

speaker: idera
text: The bottom names the size of the pieces: never add it.

speaker: idera
text: x plus 1 over 3 equals 5 over 6. x equals what?

speaker: idera
text: Multiply, don't add: 1 over 2 equals 4 over 8 because both were times 4.

speaker: idera
text: 3 of 4 equal parts are shaded. Which fraction?

speaker: idera
text: Parts you take go on top; total parts go on the bottom.

speaker: idera
text: The bottom number counts ALL the parts.

speaker: idera
text: A puff-puff is cut into 8 equal pieces. You eat 5. Fraction eaten?

speaker: idera
text: List each times table; find the first number in both.

speaker: idera
text: The product works but isn't always the smallest.

speaker: idera
text: The LCM is a multiple, so it is at least as big as both numbers.

speaker: idera
text: x plus 5 equals 12. x equals what?

speaker: idera
text: I found where your gap starts: Equivalent fractions.

speaker: idera
text: Your path back up is: Equivalent fractions, then Adding fractions (different bottoms), then Equations with fractions.

speaker: idera
text: I will send you one practice question by SMS every day, and call you again on Saturday to check your progress.

text: Sorry, I did not get that.

text: Hello Tunde! This is RootPath, calling for your weekly check on Equivalent fractions.

text: Quick reminder: Multiply top and bottom by the same number. 1 over 2 times 4 over 4 equals 4 over 8, so 1 over 2 equals 4 over 8. Never add.

text: Your level in Equivalent fractions went from 30 percent to 90 percent. Great work!

text: Press star to hear it again.

speaker: idera
text: Press 1 for Speed, distance and time.

speaker: idera
text: Press 3 for Speed with fractions of an hour.

speaker: idera
text: 6 times 7 means 6 groups of 7, not 6 plus 7.

speaker: idera
text: 12 sweets are shared equally among 3 children. Each gets?

speaker: idera
text: 18 yams go equally into 6 bags. Yams per bag?

speaker: idera
text: Which is bigger: 1 over 2 or 1 over 5?

speaker: idera
text: More pieces means smaller pieces: 1 over 5 is less than 1 over 2.

speaker: idera
text: Divide top and bottom by the same number.

speaker: idera
text: Keep dividing until no number divides both.

speaker: idera
text: Make the bottoms the same before adding.

speaker: idera
text: Top times top, bottom times bottom.

speaker: idera
text: A fraction of something is smaller: divide by the bottom.

speaker: idera
text: 3 over 4 of 20 naira notes equals what?

speaker: idera
text: Two steps: divided by bottom, then times top.

speaker: idera
text: Ada ate 1 over 2 a loaf in the morning and 1 over 4 in the afternoon. How much in all?

speaker: idera
text: 'Morning AND afternoon' means put together: add.

speaker: idera
text: Did you use every part the question gave you?

speaker: idera
text: Ada had 1 loaf. She ate 1 over 2 and then 1 over 4. How much is LEFT?

speaker: idera
text: Underline the last words of the question: used, or left?

speaker: idera
text: Ada ate 1 over 3 of a cake and Bola ate 1 over 6. Together?

speaker: idera
text: Watch the minus sign: 4 minus 7 goes below zero.

speaker: idera
text: Only add terms with the same letter: 3x and 2 are different kinds.

speaker: idera
text: x minus 4 equals 9. x equals what?

speaker: idera
text: Two steps: undo the plus or minus first, then the times.

speaker: idera
text: x minus 1 over 4 equals 1 over 2. x equals what?

speaker: idera
text: Check the unit first: km and m are distance, s and h are time, kg is mass.

speaker: idera
text: A car goes 100 km in 2 hours. Speed?

speaker: idera
text: Speed equals distance divided by time. Distance goes on top.

speaker: idera
text: A trader walks 12 km in 3 hours. Speed?

speaker: idera
text: A bus travels 90 km in 3 hours. Speed?

speaker: idera
text: F equals m times a. m equals 4 kg, a equals 3 m/s squared. F equals what?

speaker: idera
text: Force equals mass times acceleration and work equals force times distance. Multiply, never add.

speaker: idera
text: F equals m times a. m equals 5 kg, a equals 2 m/s squared. F equals what?

speaker: idera
text: F equals m times a. m equals 6 kg, a equals 4 m/s squared. F equals what?

speaker: idera
text: Work equals force times distance. 10 N over 3 m. Work?

speaker: idera
text: Work equals force times distance. 8 N over 5 m. Work?

speaker: idera
text: Work equals force times distance. 20 N over 4 m. Work?

speaker: idera
text: A cyclist rides 6 km in 1 over 2 hour. Speed?

speaker: idera
text: Dividing by 1 over 2 asks how many halves fit: 6 divided by 1 over 2 equals 12.

speaker: idera
text: A boy runs 10 km in 1 over 4 hour. Speed?

speaker: idera
text: A bike goes 15 km in 3 over 4 hour. Speed?

speaker: idera
text: A noun names a thing; a verb shows an action.

speaker: idera
text: In "Ada sells yams", the verb is:

speaker: idera
text: One person goes; many people go. The children are, my brother is.

speaker: idera
text: My brother ___ to school every day.

speaker: idera
text: Some verbs change completely: go , so went, buy , so bought.

speaker: idera
text: Last week she ___ a new phone.

speaker: idera
text: If plus present , so will (If it rains, we will stay). If plus past , so would.

speaker: idera
text: Use I for the doer (Ada and I) and me after a verb or to (to Tunde and me).

speaker: idera
text: The teacher gave a book to Tunde and ___.

speaker: idera
text: If it rains, we ___ at home.

text: If I ___ money, I would buy a car.

text: If she ___ hard, she will pass.

speaker: idera
text: Quick reminder: 6 × 7 means 6 groups of 7: 7, 14, 21, 28, 35, 42. Six bags of 7 oranges is 42 oranges.

speaker: idera
text: Quick reminder: Sharing equally is division. 12 sweets for 3 children: 12 ÷ 3 = 4 each.

speaker: idera
text: Quick reminder: The bottom counts all the equal parts; the top counts the parts you take. Eat 3 of 8 puff-puff pieces: 3/8.

speaker: idera
text: Quick reminder: Multiply top and bottom by the same number. 1/2 × 4/4 = 4/8, so 1/2 = 4/8. Never add.

speaker: idera
text: Quick reminder: Divide top and bottom by the same number until you cannot. 12/18 ÷ 6 = 2/3.

speaker: idera
text: Quick reminder: List each times table and find the first number in both. 4: 4, 8, 12. 6: 6, 12. LCM = 12.

speaker: idera
text: Quick reminder: Same bottom: add the tops, keep the bottom. 2/7 + 3/7 = 5/7.

speaker: idera
text: Quick reminder: Make the bottoms equal first. 1/2 + 1/3 = 3/6 + 2/6 = 5/6.

speaker: idera
text: Quick reminder: Top × top, bottom × bottom, then simplify. 2/3 × 3/4 = 6/12 = 1/2.

speaker: idera
text: Quick reminder: Divide by the bottom, then multiply by the top. 3/4 of 20: 20 ÷ 4 = 5, 5 × 3 = 15.

speaker: idera
text: Quick reminder: Underline what is asked: total, used or left. Then choose add or subtract.

speaker: idera
text: Quick reminder: On a number line, minus moves left. 4 − 7 = −3.

speaker: idera
text: Quick reminder: Add only terms with the same letter. 3x + 2x = 5x, but 3x + 2 stays.

speaker: idera
text: Quick reminder: Undo with the opposite. x + 5 = 12 → x = 12 − 5 = 7.

speaker: idera
text: Quick reminder: Undo plus or minus first, then times. 2x + 3 = 11 → 2x = 8 → x = 4.

speaker: idera
text: Quick reminder: Same rule, with fractions. x + 1/2 = 3/4 → x = 3/4 − 2/4 = 1/4.

speaker: idera
text: Quick reminder: Check the unit first: km and m measure distance, s and h measure time, kg measures mass. 1 km = 1000 m; 1 hour = 60 minutes.

speaker: idera
text: Quick reminder: Speed = distance ÷ time. 100 km in 2 hours: 100 ÷ 2 = 50 km/h.

speaker: idera
text: Quick reminder: Force = mass × acceleration. 4 kg at 3 m/s²: 4 × 3 = 12 N. Multiply, never add.

speaker: idera
text: Quick reminder: Work = force × distance. 10 N over 3 m: 10 × 3 = 30 J.

speaker: idera
text: Quick reminder: Dividing by a fraction asks how many fit. 6 km in 1/2 hour: 6 ÷ 1/2 = 12 km/h.

speaker: idera
text: Quick reminder: A noun names a person, place or thing (market). A verb shows action (run, sells).

speaker: idera
text: Quick reminder: The verb must match the subject: one person goes, many people go; the children are, my brother is.

speaker: idera
text: Quick reminder: Many past-tense verbs add -ed (played), but irregular ones change: go → went, buy → bought.

speaker: idera
text: Quick reminder: Use I as the doer (Ada and I went) and me after a verb or "to" (to Tunde and me).

speaker: idera
text: Quick reminder: If + present, then will: If it rains, we will stay. If + past, then would: If I had money, I would buy a car.
